fullDesc: The Raspberry Pi Pico 2 is the RP2350-powered successor to the original Pico, and it keeps everything that made the first board easy to live with — the 51 × 21 mm DIP footprint, the 40-pin breadboard-friendly layout, drag-and-drop USB flashing — while roughly doubling the compute underneath. Two Arm Cortex-M33 cores or two Hazard3 RISC-V cores (selectable at boot) run at up to 150 MHz , backed by 520 KB of on-chip SRAM and 4 MB of onboard QSPI flash. That extra headroom is what you feel in practice: larger MicroPython programs, deeper sensor buffers, floating-point and DSP maths that used to be out of reach, and several PIO-driven interfaces running at the same time. Existing Pico projects and add-on boards carry straight over, so you can move a working build onto this RP2350 microcontroller board without redesigning your wiring. Key Features ⚡ Dual-core, dual-architecture RP2350A — run two Arm Cortex-M33 cores or two Hazard3 RISC-V cores at up to 150 MHz, with an on-chip PLL for variable core frequency. 🧠 520 KB SRAM + 4 MB QSPI flash — nearly double the original Pico on both counts, with a 16 KB XIP cache so code runs from flash without stalling. 🔧 26 multi-function GPIO — 2 × UART, 2 × SPI, 2 × I2C, 16 PWM channels and 3 ADC inputs fed by a 12-bit 500 ksps converter. All IO is fixed at 3.3 V. 🎛️ 12 PIO state machines — three programmable IO blocks that let you build interfaces the chip has no dedicated peripheral for, such as SD card, VGA or addressable LED strips. 🔒 Hardware security block — Arm TrustZone for Cortex-M, signed boot, 8 KB of antifuse OTP for key storage, SHA-256 acceleration, a hardware TRNG and fast glitch detectors. 🔋 Flexible 1.8–5.5 V supply — an on-board buck-boost SMPS runs the board from micro-USB, a single Li-ion cell or 3 × AA in series, so battery projects need no extra regulator. 📏 Breadboard or surface-mount — 51 × 21 mm, 1 mm thick PCB on a 2.54 mm (0.1″) grid, with castellated edges so the same board can be reflow-soldered as a module. 🛠️ Easy to program and debug — drag-and-drop UF2 over micro-USB, plus a 3-pin ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) header for real breakpoint debugging. ✅ C/C++ and MicroPython — a mature SDK, thousands of examples and full documentation, backed by production until at least January 2040. fullDesc: The 13N60 MOSFET is a widely used power field-effect transistor known for its high voltage rating and robust performance in switching applications. This article provides a comprehensive overview of the 13N60 MOSFET, including its specifications, typical use cases, and comparisons with similar MOSFETs such as the 65N06, 7N60, 15N60, and others. Whether you're designing a power supply, motor control system, or high-voltage switching circuit, understanding the 13N60 MOSFET is essential for making an informed selection. When users search for “13N60 MOSFET,” the primary intent is to find a reliable power transistor suitable for high-voltage applications. This search often comes from engineers or hobbyists working on projects that require efficient switching at voltages up to 600V. The 13N60 is a popular choice due to its ability to handle high voltages while maintaining low on-resistance, which minimizes power loss and heat generation. To better understand how to use the 13N60 MOSFET in a practical scenario, consider the following example: You are designing a high-voltage DC-DC converter that requires a MOSFET capable of handling 600V and at least 13A of continuous current. The 13N60 is a suitable candidate for this application. Here’s how to evaluate and implement it: Determine the voltage and current requirements of your circuit to ensure the 13N60 meets the necessary specifications. Check the thermal characteristics, including thermal resistance and maximum junction temperature, to ensure proper heat dissipation. Review the gate threshold voltage and switching speed to ensure compatibility with your control circuitry. Compare the 13N60 with similar MOSFETs such as the 15N60, 20N60, and 40N60 to determine the best fit for your application. 13N60 MOSFET A power MOSFET with a 600V drain-source voltage rating and a continuous drain current of 13A, suitable for high-voltage switching applications. Gate Threshold Voltage (V GS(th) ) The minimum voltage required at the gate to begin conducting current between the drain and source. fullDesc: The UNI-T UT139C is a digital multimeter that offers a wide range of measurement capabilities for both professionals and hobbyists. It is designed to provide accurate and reliable readings for various electrical parameters. Here is a description of the features and specifications of the UNI-T UT139C: Display: The multimeter features a large, easy-to-read digital LCD display that shows the measured values clearly. The display is backlit, allowing for easy reading in low-light conditions. Measurement Functions: The UT139C offers a comprehensive set of measurement functions, including voltage (both AC and DC), current (AC and DC), resistance, capacitance, frequency, duty cycle, temperature, diode testing, and continuity testing. Auto and Manual Ranging: The multimeter supports both auto-ranging and manual-ranging modes. In auto-ranging mode, the device automatically selects the appropriate range for the measured quantity, simplifying the measurement process. Manual ranging allows the user to manually select the desired range for more control. True RMS: The UT139C is equipped with True RMS (Root Mean Square) technology, which ensures accurate measurements of AC voltage and current, even for non-sinusoidal waveforms. Data Hold and Relative Mode: The multimeter features a data hold function that allows the user to freeze the displayed value for easy reading and recording. The relative mode enables the user to measure the difference between two values, useful for zeroing out test leads or comparing readings. Input Protection: The multimeter has built-in overload protection for all ranges, safeguarding it from accidental damage due to excessive voltage or current. Connectivity: The UT139C comes with a standard input jack for connecting the test leads. It also has a built-in low battery indicator to alert the user when the battery needs replacement. Design and Build: The multimeter is designed with ergonomics in mind, featuring a rugged construction with a protective rubber holster that provides durability and impact resistance. The device is compact and lightweight, making it portable and easy to handle. Power Supply: The UT139C is powered by standard AA batteries, providing convenience and flexibility in terms of power source. Overall, the UNI-T UT139C is a versatile and reliable digital multimeter that offers a wide range of measurement functions and features....

The board has 2 × 20 pin headers, providing 28 additional programmable GPIO pins.
